transcript:
This is NPR News now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump has landed in China, where he will stay for only about 24 hours.
High stakes meetings with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin are on
the agenda for Trump's visit, which is his second to China this year.
NPR's Deepa Shivaram reports.
After meeting with allies in Manila, Trump is headed into major summits with adversaries.
Relations between the U.S. and China have cooled since last year, when Trump and Xi
met in South Korea amid an escalating trade war.
The two nations still share tension, though, over access to rare earths and AI chips.
The meeting between Trump and Xi is not expected to deliver much that is new, but their consistent
meetings this year help solidify a more stable relationship, analysts say.
Both leaders will meet again next month in Miami, where Trump is hosting the G20 summit.
Deepa Shivaram and PR News Shenzhen.
The Associated Press has called the last outstanding Senate race in Alaska for Democratic challenger
Mary Peltola.
She flipped the ninth Republican-held Senate seat this cycle by defeating incumbent Dan
Sullivan, and PR's Eric McDaniel has more.
Peltola ran a campaign squarely centered on Alaskan issues, fish, family and freedom.
The moderate Democrat previously served in Congress as Alaska's sole House member.
Her Senate race was a controversial one.
The New York Times spoke to a former campaign staffer who alleged Democrats recruited a
man with the same name as her opponent into the race.
She denies involvement, and NPR has not independently confirmed the allegations.
Peltola's race is the final Senate race to be called.
Democrats will control the chamber, 56 to 44.
NPR's Eric McDaniel reporting.
The Federal Aviation Administration says it will temporarily stop using the types of routers
involved in last Friday's technical meltdown in the nation's air traffic control system,
and PR's Joe Hernandez has more.
The government contractor L3 Harris was installing the router at a site in Arkansas just before
the technical disruptions began.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said 68 of these routers had been installed previously
without incident.
This is the one that started to behave this way.
So we thought it's only prudent to pause the use of these routers.
L3 Harris sent the routers involved in Friday's incident to its lab in Florida, where officials
with the FAA and the FBI are also on site.
Duffy says there's no indication the malfunction was the result of a cyberattack, but that
the investigation is ongoing.
Joe Hernandez, NPR News.
Last hour, the space probe Voyager 1 achieved an astonishing record.
NASA says it is now one full light day away from Earth.
It's about 16 billion miles, or the same as how long it takes light to travel in 24 hours.
Voyager 1 is now the farthest away from Earth than any human-made object has ever traveled.
You're listening to NPR.
The National Weather Service says another Pacific storm is hitting the California coast.
It is powered by the weather pattern known as El Nino, and it will likely create flooding
conditions in some California areas.
It has also triggered massive waves.
Some have reached at least 30 feet high.
From member station KQED, Ezra David Romero has more.
In Pacifica, south of San Francisco, the powerful waves crashed into the back of Lou Raven's
Weathered Red Home, which sits just a few feet from the Pacific Ocean.
He was out of town when the waves hit, and he was relieved to find his house still standing
when he returned.
"There's some minor things.
All in all, it's held up.
99%.
I've been very lucky that the house is still here."
The large waves are expected to churn up the coastline again later this week as a series
of storms hits the region.
Climate scientists are worried a storm, big waves, higher seas and king tides could create
major flooding around Thanksgiving.
For NPR News, I'm Ezra David Romero in San Francisco.
The winners of the National Book Awards will be announced tonight.
Categories range from fiction to poetry, young people's literature to translated works.
The National Book Foundation will also honor novelist Salman Rushdie.
He was badly injured in a stabbing attack in 2022.
Rushdie will receive the Medal for Distinguished Contribution to American Letters.
I'm Cora Vekulman, NPR News, from Washington.

topics.text: Trump lands in China for a roughly 24-hour visit with Xi Jinping and Putin meetings
Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate race, giving Democrats control of the Senate 56-44
FAA pauses use of L3 Harris routers after last Friday's air traffic control technical meltdown
Voyager 1 becomes one full light day from Earth, farthest human-made object ever
Powerful Pacific storm and massive waves hit California coast, causing damage in Pacifica
National Book Awards to be announced tonight; Salman Rushdie to receive medal for distinguished contribution
